title: Stop Killing Games fails to secure EU law despite 1.3M signatures
summary: The Stop Killing Games campaign, which aimed to establish EU legislation protecting gamers' rights to continue playing purchased games after server shutdowns, failed to secure legal protection despite gathering over 1.3 million signatures on the European Citizens' Initiative, falling short of the threshold needed to mandate EU Commission action.
problem_solved: Addresses the issue of gamers losing permanent access to legally purchased digital games when publishers shut down servers or abandon titles.
why_valuable: Highlights the growing tension between digital ownership rights and gaming industry practices, while demonstrating the limitations of grassroots political movements in affecting tech regulation.
